items.title: Who Pays the Referees
items.content_text: Every party that checks frontier AI depends on the labs it checks for access, compute, money or the right to publish. A ledger of which of those terms are public, party by party, with Anthropic first.

items.title: Who Knew First
items.content_text: An op-ed and the record behind it. By the record's account, the organization that ran the model held the decisive facts in each of nine AI agent incidents from 2026, and in six of them someone else told the public first.

items.title: The Number Has a Vintage
items.content_text: An official jobs estimate changes as later data arrive. Each version answers a different question, and a fair comparison names which one it uses.

items.title: Frontier Safety briefing
items.content_text: A dated monitor of AISI, Anthropic, OpenAI and industry safety records. Each edition keeps reported facts, source roles and limits apart.

items.title: What the Formula Counts
items.content_text: A readability score measures selected text features. Comprehension, audience fit and accessibility require evidence of their own.

items.title: The Timestamp Is Not the Order
items.content_text: Precise-looking timestamps need clock-error evidence and ordering relations before they can support a close sequence of events.

items.title: The Scene the Song Did Not Tell You
items.content_text: Music-evoked stories can share patterns while retaining personal meaning. Those reports do not by themselves demonstrate creative accomplishment.

items.title: Support Has More Than One Record
items.content_text: A helper’s report, a recipient’s account and a measured outcome answer different questions about whether support worked.

items.title: What the Label Changes
items.content_text: A label can change where people look and how easily they make sense of an artwork, without raising liking, learning, accuracy or artistic value.

items.title: The Second Hearing
items.content_text: Repeated listening changes liking, prediction, attention and memory in different ways. A replay count records exposure and says nothing about quality.

items.title: The Sandbox Was Never Just a Box
items.content_text: Separate security reports expose a shared question: what can an agent reach, and can the instruments that record its actions remain trustworthy?

items.title: LTJ Bukem: The Man Behind the Atmosphere
items.content_text: Danny Williamson’s calm, spacious records come out of a series of musical decisions, shaped by his taste and working habits and by the musicians around him.

items.title: Borrowed Ground
items.content_text: On existence and what our work owes other people.

items.title: An open letter on checking the machines
items.content_text: A signed letter to the people who build AI systems: a person should be able to question a machine's answer without first winning an argument with its owner.

items.title: A witness should not become a ruler
items.content_text: An expanded essay on the public tool portfolio, contribution from outside academia, evidence for review and changing educational practice.

items.title: Growth Needs a Before
items.content_text: Feeling changed after trauma can matter on its own. Measuring lasting change asks for a before, an after, and clear limits on what the score can prove.

items.title: Availability Is Not Reach
items.content_text: Tutoring has strong trial evidence. Public claims about a program must keep its availability, reach, dosage, staffing and outcomes as separate facts.

items.title: Five evidence lanes, one OpenAI and Hugging Face incident
items.content_text: Separate legal process, OpenAI's company report, Hugging Face host telemetry, independent analysis, and vendor remediation before drawing conclusions from the July incident.
